quotes.text: People ask me, 'Freddie, where do you find your confidence?' Darling, I woke up on a tour bus in Stuttgart with a feather boa around my neck, someone else's boots on my feet, and a half-eaten crêpe on my chest — and I still walked onstage and blew the roof off the place. Confidence isn't found. It's what's left when you've run out of anything sensible to feel.

quotes.context: BBC Radio 1 Rock Week interview with Tommy Vance, broadcast October 1984, recorded backstage at the Birmingham NEC following the Works Tour warm-up date

quotes.text: Comedy is very simple. You find the thing a room full of people are all privately thinking and you say it out loud as fast as possible before your brain catches up and tells you not to. That's the whole job. Everything else is just lighting and a microphone and hoping the bar tab isn't yours.

quotes.text: The rider said 'no brown M&Ms' and everyone thinks that's ego. It's not ego. Ego is what I do onstage. The M&M thing is just QA. If the bowl's got brown ones in it, nobody read the contract, and if nobody read that page, nobody read the page about the weight limits on the stage rigging either, and then somebody gets hurt. Brown M&Ms save lives. I'm basically a safety officer with better trousers.
